thread:
oliver_martin: SummitBridge POC kickoff. Customer requests a drop-in replacement for vendor-old /v1/respond with minimal client changes. Success criteria: prompt parity, deterministic diffs for QA, and a predictable migration billing model (21 days). Need SE + Security + Finance. Timeline = 2 weeks.

zoe_khan: Quick q — do we have their sample corpus? chat arrays vs single-prompt matters for token accounting. Also what's their target p95?

oliver_martin: Corpus is on the onboarding drive (~650 examples). Mostly message arrays, a small tail of single-prompt calls. They listed 250ms p95 as ideal, will accept up to 600ms in peak windows.

jessica_yu: Proposed POC plan (short):
1) Small compat shim that accepts Vendor envelope and translates to Redwood chat/generation API.
2) Deterministic harness: temperature=0, top_p=1, seed-lock where available.
3) Response-normalizer to strip vendor metadata, canonicalize dates/currency, and standardize whitespace.
4) Run ~1k A/B pairs to produce semantic similarity, token-delta, and billing-delta reports. I'll own harness + normalization.

mike_chen: Example shim mapping to share with their engineers:
```
# incoming vendor-old request
POST /v1/respond
{ "prompt": "List recent charges for acct 42", "max_tokens": 180 }
# shim -> Redwood chat/generate
POST /v1/chat.complete
{ "model": "redwood-chat-1", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "List recent charges for acct 42"}], "max_tokens": 180, "temperature": 0 }
```
This keeps the client call surface nearly identical and forces deterministic sampling for parity runs.

security-bot: staging environment "summitbridge-poc-eu" provisioned in eu-west-1. Firewall/allowlist template created.

zoe_khan: Security checklist: EU data residency required, BYOK via Azure Key Vault requested, 12-month audit log retention, signed DPA, and pen-test evidence. Need allowlist IPs and contact at their security team to exchange SAs.

mike_chen: Pricing note: customer prefers a flat migration price for the cutover to avoid token surprises. Propose a 21-day flat-rate option and a tokenized long-term projection. I'll draft a quote: sample flat-rate $0.0175 per call for up to 300k calls; will include a spreadsheet with 3 representative requests (low/med/high) and token breakdowns.

jessica_yu: For the normalizer I'll include a canonicalizer that: removes vendor-debug fields, normalizes numeric/currency formats (ISO date, 2-decimal currency), strips extra whitespace, and applies a small schema (title/body/metadata). This usually reduces false-positive deltas in semantic checks.

oliver_martin: Can we schedule a smoke on Tue 07:00 CET? Customer prefers early window.

security-bot: allowlist placeholders added to the staging firewall; awaiting customer IPs.

zoe_khan: Blockers from security: Azure KV EU-only CMK requirement may push them to Dedicated/Private; DPA signature and explicit KMS flow docs required. If those are satisfied, no additional security blockers.

mike_chen: I'll provision a small staging model instance, wire the shim, and post deploy/rollback steps here when ready. Also will capture tokenization differences (Vendor vs Redwood) for finance. If we see token inflation, recommendation will be quantized model variant + batching.

jessica_yu: Will run the A/B harness and post a diff report with: embedding-based semantic similarity, token delta, top-3 failure cases (formatting, truncation, hallucination), and suggested canonicalizer rules.

oliver_martin: Action items: 1) jessica: ship harness + normalization; 2) mike: flat-rate quote + staging instructions; 3) zoe: security Qs + docs; 4) infra/security-bot: finalize allowlist and firewall. I'll notify the customer and send calendar invite for Tuesday smoke. Marking thread active.

mike_chen: PR link and deploy instructions to follow.

jessica_yu: Posting initial A/B smoke results by EOD today (100-sample run).

oliver_martin: Any other enterprise blockers?

zoe_khan: One more ask from their infra team: per-request correlation-id forwarded to their SIEM via syslog. Confirming if staging pipeline can stream filtered audit events to customer syslog.

mike_chen: We can export a filtered audit stream to their syslog in staging (syslog-ng connector); will need allowlist IPs and syslog endpoint.

oliver_martin: Great. Thanks team. Thread remains active.
